artifacts.summary: Diagnoses Piece 1 (heartbeat silence) as a confirmed design gap -- 11 of 13 domain implementation agents never call update-phase-status.sh, bypassing the mechanized heartbeat -- verified against live BimodalLogic evidence; scopes Piece 2 (third lock state) via session_liveness() consumption keyed on session_id; scopes Piece 3 (registry file_scope re-derivation on heartbeat) as a small extraction fix; confirms both absorbed defects (dead Class E review, stale batch-size message) and resolves the dead-session-registry-entries question as already correctly handled (no action needed).

memory_candidates.content: In this agent system, a mechanized fix embedded inside a shared script (e.g. update-phase-status.sh's heartbeat refresh) only reaches callers that actually invoke that script. When ~13 structurally parallel domain agent files (lean/typst/latex/etc *-implementation-agent.md) each independently document their own phase-heading mutation instructions, migrating only one (general-implementation-agent.md) to call the new script leaves every other agent silently uncovered -- the original prose-reliability bug reappears in a sibling file rather than being fixed system-wide. Always grep all agent files for the pattern being replaced, not just the one being edited.

task-lock.sh's session_liveness() (factored out for cmd_session_list/session_contention) is the canonical, already-tested liveness vocabulary (corrupt, dead-pid, dead-pid-within-grace, stale-heartbeat, pid-alive, undeterminable) for this codebase. Any new liveness-sensitive decision (e.g. a per-task lock's stale-but-pid-alive state) should consume this function via a session_id-keyed lookup into specs/.sessions/<session_id>.json, never by comparing pids directly against the caller -- pid_source can be 'ancestor-claude' for two genuinely different /orchestrate sessions sharing one Claude Code process ancestry, so pid-equality self-exclusion silently disables cross-session detection for the most common concurrency shape.

Before treating a dispatch-text 'ALSO OBSERVED' or 'argue, don't assume' open question as requiring a code change, grep for the suspected-missing wiring directly -- skill-refresh/SKILL.md and commands/refresh.md already called task-lock.sh session-reap on explicit /refresh invocation, resolving what looked like an open reap-policy design question as already-correct, no-action-needed. Dispatch prose can be stale relative to the current codebase even when carefully evidenced.
